name: Meeting management agent
description:
---

**Use cases are many:** Let users book, check, reschedule, or cancel meetings directly from Telegram. Perfect for solopreneurs, agencies, or teams who want an AI-powered assistant that prevents double-bookings, manages Google Calendar, and even sends email invites automatically.

---

**Good to know**
At time of writing, this workflow uses **OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini** for natural conversation handling. See [OpenAI Pricing](https://openai.com/pricing) for updated info.
This workflow relies on **Google Calendar** for scheduling — if the model says “conflict found,” it means an event already exists in that time slot.

---

**How it works**

* **Telegram Chat**: A user types natural requests like “Book a meeting with Sarah tomorrow at 2 PM” or “Do I have meetings on Friday?”.
* **AI Agent (OpenAI)**: Interprets the request, calculates dates (using Date & Time), and decides whether to create, update, or delete a meeting.
* **Conflict Checking**: Before booking, the agent checks Google Calendar for existing events to avoid overlaps.
* **Meeting Management**:

  * **Create**: Adds new events with title, description, attendees.
  * **Update**: Edits existing events.
  * **Delete**: Cancels meetings if requested.
  * **Get**: Lists all meetings for a date or time range.
* **Notifications**: Replies instantly on Telegram and, if needed, sends a Gmail email with meeting details.
* **Memory**: Keeps context of the conversation so users can speak naturally (“reschedule that meeting to 4 PM instead”).

---

**How to use**

* Start a Telegram chat with the bot.
* Type a request in plain English (no need for structured inputs).
* The agent will confirm or suggest alternatives if a conflict exists.
* Meetings appear in Google Calendar and details can be emailed via Gmail.

---

**Requirements**

* Telegram bot connected to n8n
* OpenAI API key (for AI-driven scheduling assistant)
* Google Calendar account (for event creation & conflict checking)
* Gmail account (for sending invites & confirmations)

---

**Customising this workflow**

* Add support for multiple calendars (work, personal, shared).
* Change the conflict-resolution logic (e.g., auto-suggest nearest free slot).
* Include recurring meetings (weekly standups, monthly reviews).
* Add Slack or WhatsApp integration for multi-platform scheduling.
* Extend Gmail invites with calendar attachments (.ics files).

---

👉 [Rakin Jakaria](https://www.youtube.com/@RakinJakaria)

options.systemMessage:
=You are a smart, helpful AI assistant that helps users schedule meetings, check availability, create events in Google Calendar, and send meeting details via email.
Always respond like a friendly, professional human assistant.

Core Process:

ALWAYS use Date and Time tool FIRST to get current date/time
ALWAYS check Google Calendar for conflicts before booking new meetings
Only create meetings if no time conflicts exist

Critical Rules:

Date Accuracy: When user says "tomorrow," "next Monday," etc., use Date and Time tool to calculate exact dates.

Conflict Prevention: Before creating any meeting, check if user already has something booked at that time. If conflict exists, inform user and offer alternatives.

Never double-book: Always resolve conflicts before creating new meetings.

Tool Usage:

Date and Time tool: Use first to establish current date, then for any relative date calculations

Google Calendar tool: Check for conflicts first, then create events only if no conflicts

Gmail tool: Use when user asks to send meeting details or email invites

Example Workflows:

Booking Request: "Book meeting with Sarah tomorrow at 2 PM"

Get current date → Calculate tomorrow's exact date
Check calendar for that time slot
If no conflict: Create meeting / If conflict: "You already have [meeting] at 2 PM on [date]. Different time?"

Meeting Inquiry: "Do I have meetings tomorrow?"

Get current date → Calculate tomorrow's exact date
Search calendar for that date
List meetings with specific date: "Here are your meetings for [exact date]:"


Be proactive. Make scheduling easy and human-like. Don’t ask the user to write structured inputs — understand what they mean naturally.

---

# 🛠 Setup Guide

Follow these steps to get started:

1. **Connect your [Telegram Bot](https://core.telegram.org/bots#creating-a-new-bot)**

   * In the **Telegram Trigger** and **Telegram** nodes, insert your Telegram bot token (from @BotFather).
   * This allows users to chat with the agent directly from Telegram.

2. **Add your [OpenAI](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys) API key**

   * Used in the **OpenAI** node to power natural conversation and interpret scheduling requests.
   * Choose the right model (`gpt-4.1-mini` is already set).

3. **Enable Conversation Memory**

   * The **Memory** node is linked to Telegram chat IDs, so the bot remembers ongoing conversations.
   * No extra setup needed, but make sure the session key remains `chat.id`.

4. **Plug in your [Google Calendar](https://calendar.google.com/) account**

   * In the **Get**, **Update**, **Delete**, and **Create** nodes, connect your Google Calendar.
   * This lets the AI check availability, prevent double-booking, and create events.

5. **Set your Timezone**

   * In the **Date & Time** node, confirm your correct timezone (currently `Asia/Dhaka`).
   * This ensures correct handling of “tomorrow,” “next Monday,” etc.

6. **Connect your [Gmail](https://mail.google.com/) account**

   * In the **Gmail** node, link your Gmail account.
   * This is used to send meeting invites and confirmations to attendees.

7. **AI Agent System Message (already set)**

   * The **AI Agent** node has rules to:

     * Always calculate exact dates with Date & Time
     * Always check calendar before creating events
     * Avoid double-booking and suggest alternatives
   * Keep these rules as they make the assistant act professional and human-like.

Once all connections are set, your workflow will **chat with users on Telegram, check Google Calendar for availability, create meetings, and send invites via Gmail — all automatically** 📅🤖
